title: DayRecall — AI memory for your whole day | Apple Watch & iPhone
description: DayRecall listens on Apple Watch or iPhone during the hours you choose, turns what was said into text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day.
og_title: DayRecall — AI memory for your whole day
og_description: Your Apple Watch, or just your iPhone, listens during the hours you choose and keeps what was said as text. Ask about your day any time.
og_image_alt: DayRecall: AI memory for your whole day. Best with Apple Watch, works with iPhone alone.
app_description: An AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone. During the hours you choose it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words.
app_features: Listens all day on Apple Watch, with no iPhone nearby; works with iPhone alone too
Speech becomes text on the iPhone; no audio is kept
Ask about your day and get the exact words, with the moment they were said
Marks who said what: Me, Other 1, Other 2
Follows conversations in up to three languages, translated into yours
Picks out to-dos, deadlines and meetings for you to confirm

Optional Health clues: inputs used by the App are kept in a protected local cache; Health labels and values are included in a recap sent to your API or a day shared with an AI app only if you choose to add them
No account and no DayRecall server; to-dos, recaps and answers use this iPhone by default, or your own API after you configure it and allow sharing

items.q: What is DayRecall?
items.a: DayRecall is an AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone, made for people who forget things. During the hours you choose, it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words and where they came from.

items.q: Do I need an Apple Watch?
items.a: No. DayRecall works best with Apple Watch, and your iPhone can also listen on its own. When both listen, your day is one timeline, and what both heard is shown once.

items.q: Does DayRecall keep audio recordings?
items.a: No. What’s said is turned into text on your iPhone, and the audio is cleared automatically once it’s transcribed. Only the text is kept.

items.q: Where is my data, and who can see it?
items.a: Your data is stored on your iPhone and in backups you choose to make. There is no account and no DayRecall server receiving your day. To-dos, recaps and answers use this iPhone by default. If you select and allow your own API, it receives new transcripts automatically for to-dos, a day’s conversations when you request a recap, and questions with matching excerpts. It may first receive a question alone to help search. You can also share a selected day with an AI app. These recipients use their own privacy rules; audio is never sent to the API.

items.q: What do I need to use DayRecall?
items.a: An iPhone with iOS 26 or later that supports Apple’s on-device speech recognition. An Apple Watch with watchOS 26 or later is optional. To-dos, recaps and answers use one AI engine: this iPhone’s model, which requires Apple Intelligence, or an OpenAI-compatible API that you configure and allow. Your API needs an internet connection.

items.q: Which iPhone models work?
items.a: DayRecall needs iOS 26 or later, which runs on iPhone 11 and later and iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later. Turning speech into text also needs Apple’s on-device speech recognition, which Apple doesn’t offer on some older models, including iPhone 11 models and iPhone SE (2nd generation), so we recommend iPhone 12 or later. If your iPhone can’t transcribe, DayRecall tells you. For to-dos, recaps and answers, the On this iPhone engine needs a device that supports Apple Intelligence. My own API can perform those three tasks without Apple Intelligence; transcription still requires the on-device speech recognition described above.

items.q: Which Apple Watch models work?
items.a: Any Apple Watch that runs watchOS 26 or later: Apple Watch Series 6 and later, Apple Watch SE (2nd generation) and later, and every Apple Watch Ultra. It needs to be paired with an iPhone that runs DayRecall. Apple Watch is optional: your iPhone can listen on its own.

items.q: Does my iPhone have to stay near my watch?
items.a: No. Your Apple Watch holds what it heard and hands it to your iPhone every two hours, or as soon as the two reconnect, for example when you get home in the evening.

items.q: Does it work without an internet connection?
items.a: Listening and transcription run on your devices. With On this iPhone selected and its required models downloaded and available, to-dos, recaps and answers also work offline. My own API needs an internet connection for those AI tasks. Places on the map also need a connection.

items.q: Why do the supported languages depend on Apple?
items.a: Transcription uses Apple’s on-device speech recognition, and translation uses Apple’s translation; their supported languages depend on the iPhone and iOS version. For to-dos, recaps and answers, On this iPhone uses Apple Intelligence and its supported languages. With My own API, language support depends on the service and model you choose. Choosing an API does not change transcription or translation support.

items.q: Which languages can DayRecall transcribe?
items.a: You can choose from English (US, UK), Chinese (Mandarin, China mainland), Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Cantonese (China mainland), Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil, Portugal), Dutch, Swedish, Danish and Turkish. Each works only if Apple’s on-device speech recognition supports it on your iPhone; if it doesn’t, DayRecall marks the language as not supported. The first time you use a language, iOS downloads its speech model.

items.q: Which languages can it translate?
items.a: Lines in your other working languages can be translated into your main language with Apple’s on-device translation, so a pair of languages can be translated only if Apple supports it on your iPhone. Transcription support does not guarantee translation support, including for Cantonese. Check the available language pairs in DayRecall’s translation settings. iOS downloads each language before its first use. Apple lists the current languages on its feature availability page.

items.q: Which languages work for to-dos, recaps and answers?
items.a: It depends on the AI engine. On this iPhone uses Apple Intelligence, so its device, language and region requirements apply. If Apple Intelligence is unavailable, including where Apple does not offer it, you can choose My own API for all three tasks: to-dos, recaps and answers. Its supported languages depend on the service and model you choose. See Apple’s guide for the current Apple Intelligence requirements.

items.q: Which languages is the app in?
items.a: The app’s menus and screens come in 14 languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Portugal), Spanish, Swedish and Turkish. This is separate from the languages it can transcribe.

items.q: Can it follow a conversation in more than one language?
items.a: Yes. Turn on Multilingual transcription and add up to two more working languages: DayRecall follows a conversation that switches between them and transcribes each part in the language it was spoken in. Lines in the other languages can then be translated into your main language.

items.q: How do I start and stop listening?
items.a: Set your listening hours once, for example workdays from 9:00 to 18:00. When they begin, your Apple Watch asks whether to start: one tap, and it stops on its own when they end. You can also stop early, or skip a day.

items.q: What can I ask?
items.a: Anything about your day, in your own words: “What did Sam promise me today?” or “When is the report due?” Each answer shows where it came from, down to the line that was said.

items.q: How do to-dos work?
items.a: DayRecall picks out promises, deadlines and meetings from your day and waits for you to confirm them. Nothing reaches your calendar or Reminders until you say yes.

items.q: How does DayRecall tell voices apart?
items.a: Turn on Mark who is speaking and read five short cards aloud, about a minute. From then on, your lines are marked Me, and everyone else in a conversation gets a number: Other 1, Other 2 and so on. Your voiceprint stays on your iPhone, and no one else’s is kept. The feature is optional and off by default.

items.q: Can I hand a day to my own AI app?
items.a: Yes. Open Recap your day from Today, a past day or Ask. Write it here uses the AI engine you selected in Settings. To use another app, choose Hand to an AI app… and select it in the system share sheet; only the conversations you leave included go into the text file. To bring its to-dos back, copy the AI’s answer and tap Bring the AI’s answer back.

items.q: Can I import an audio file?
items.a: Yes. Import an audio file and DayRecall turns it into text on your iPhone, like everything else. It works on its own copy, so your original file stays as it is.

items.q: How much battery does it use?
items.a: Very little. Our in-house ultra-light speech model keeps only the moments when someone is talking. In internal testing on Apple Watch Series 11, listening added about 0.9% battery per hour.

items.q: How soon does the text appear?
items.a: Your watch hands over what it heard about every two hours, and when it stops listening, and your iPhone turns it into text as it arrives. For text sooner, open DayRecall and tap Sync now. In internal testing on iPhone 17 Pro Max, 3 minutes of conversation were processed in 17 seconds.

items.q: Does anything leave my iPhone?
items.a: With your own API selected and sharing allowed, new transcripts are sent automatically in batches to find to-dos, even when you are not asking questions. Write it here sends the selected day’s conversations to that service for a recap, including recorded places if present and Health labels and values only if you choose to add them. Questions send the question and matching excerpts; the question may first be sent alone to help search. Audio and your voiceprint are never sent to the API. You can also share a day with an AI app. Apple Maps and backups have their own data flows, explained in the Privacy Policy.

items.q: Does DayRecall read my Health data?
items.a: Only if you turn it on in Settings › Health. DayRecall reads sleep, steps and walking distance, workouts and heart rate to label parts of your day and find the times of activities you ask about. It never writes to Health or sends the inputs to us. Inputs used by the App are kept in a protected local cache, which can be included in a password-encrypted manual backup you create. On the recap and hand-over page, Add health data is off by default. Turning it on asks for permission and your choice is remembered. With it on, Health labels and activity times are included in a recap sent to your API or a day shared with an AI app; available heart rate, step, distance and duration values are included. Missing readings are left out. Health records are not attached to to-do or question requests. No medical conclusions or health advice are given.

items.q: Does DayRecall track me or show ads?
items.a: No. DayRecall has no ads, no analytics, no tracking and no third-party code that collects data. To help fix problems, it keeps a log on your devices of what it did, never what was said, for up to 14 days; the log leaves your iPhone only if you share it.

items.q: How do I delete my data?
items.a: Delete a recording, with its text and to-dos, from its page, or everything with Settings › Privacy › Delete all memories. Delete my voice removes your voiceprint. Deleting the app removes what it stored on your devices; copies in earlier backups stay until those backups are replaced.

items.q: Do I need to tell people DayRecall is listening?
items.a: Yes. Tell the people you talk with. Some places require everyone’s consent even when only text is kept, so follow the rules where you are; that responsibility is yours, as our Terms of Service explain.

items.q: How does the Mac app work with iPhone and Apple Watch?
items.a: Mac can record an in-person meeting or your microphone and a selected meeting app. Automatic transcription requires a supported Mac with macOS 26 or later. Pair your own iPhone to share saved text, meeting notes, titles, task updates and device status over an encrypted local network; keep both apps open. Audio assistance is enabled separately, and iCloud sharing is optional. Mac audio is removed after its transcript is saved; failed transcription keeps audio for retry.

items.q: How can I back up my library?
items.a: In Settings, export a local library file or use the optional private iCloud backup. The local file has no password and can include saved Health and Calendar inputs, so store it somewhere you trust. The in-app iCloud backup excludes these inputs and saved recaps. Restoring replaces the current library and supported settings. Deleting local data does not delete exported files or cloud copies; remove those separately.

items.q: Can I save a recap to Notion or Obsidian?
items.a: Set up a destination in Settings › Third-party connections, then choose and confirm it on a saved recap. Nothing is sent automatically. Notion receives the recap directly to create a child page. Obsidian uses a device-only clipboard copy that expires after two minutes and opens a dated note; check Obsidian to confirm it was saved. Disconnecting or deleting a recap in DayRecall does not delete copies already in those apps.

items.q: When can I get DayRecall?
items.a: DayRecall is in beta and coming soon to the App Store.

items.q: How do I get help?
items.a: Write to support@dayrecall.com and tell us when it happened and on which device. A log helps most: Settings › Developer options › Logs › Share log.

steps.c: Type a question about anything you recorded, or tap one of the suggestions.
The answer comes from your recordings. Each number points to the recording it came from.
